words.enDefinition: feel less healthy than usual without naming a specific problem

examples.en: I started to feel unwell during my afternoon lecture and went home early.
examples.zh: 下午上课时我开始「感觉不舒服」，就提前回家了。

examples.en: I always feel unwell in the mornings, but by lunchtime I feel fine.
examples.zh: 我早上总「感觉不舒服」，但到了午饭时间就没事了。

words.enDefinition: feel weak and tired for some time

examples.en: I began to feel run-down toward the end of the exam period.
examples.zh: 到考试周快结束时，我开始「感觉疲惫没精神」。

examples.en: Even on days when I sleep well, I still feel run-down by midafternoon.
examples.zh: 哪怕晚上睡得好，到了下午我还是「感觉疲惫没精神」。

words.enDefinition: a feeling of tiredness that makes normal activities harder

examples.en: The nurse asked when the fatigue started and whether it affected my classes.
examples.zh: 护士问「疲劳乏力」是从什么时候开始的，是否影响了上课。

examples.en: By the afternoon, the fatigue makes it difficult for me to study.
examples.zh: 到了下午，「疲劳乏力」让我很难继续学习。

words.enDefinition: a widespread lack of strength rather than weakness in one area

examples.en: I reported general weakness because even carrying my bag to class felt difficult.
examples.zh: 我说自己「全身无力」，连背着包去上课都觉得吃力。

examples.en: The doctor asked if the general weakness was present even when I stayed in bed.
examples.zh: 医生问我躺在床上时是否也「全身无力」。

words.enDefinition: a feeling of being close to falling asleep

examples.en: The drowsiness is worst after lunch, especially during lectures in warm rooms.
examples.zh: 「困倦」在午饭后最明显，尤其是在温暖的教室里听课时。

examples.en: I noticed drowsiness every afternoon for several days before my appointment last week.
examples.zh: 上周看诊前，我连续几天下午都觉得「困倦」。

words.enDefinition: having less desire to eat than you normally do

examples.en: The loss of appetite began on Monday, when I left most of my dinner untouched.
examples.zh: 「食欲减退」是星期一开始的，那天我晚饭几乎没动。

examples.en: I mentioned the loss of appetite when the nurse asked about my eating habits.
examples.zh: 护士问我平常怎么吃饭时，我提到了「食欲减退」。

words.enDefinition: feel hot or chilled as though you have a fever

examples.en: I started to feel feverish during class, but I didn't have a thermometer.
examples.zh: 上课时我开始「感觉像在发烧」，但手边没有体温计。

examples.en: I feel feverish in the evening, though I usually feel better by morning.
examples.zh: 我晚上「感觉像在发烧」，不过通常早上会好些。

words.enDefinition: have a body temperature above its normal range

examples.en: I tend to run a fever late in the evening and feel cooler by morning.
examples.zh: 我往往深夜会「发烧」，到了早上感觉就没那么热了。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether I still run a fever as often as last week.
examples.zh: 护士问我现在是不是还像上周那么频繁地「发烧」。

collocations: run a fever for two days

words.enDefinition: a fever with a comparatively small rise in temperature

examples.en: I had a low-grade fever yesterday, but my temperature was normal this morning.
examples.zh: 我昨天有「低烧」，不过今天早上体温正常了。

examples.en: The doctor asked when I last recorded a low-grade fever at home.
examples.zh: 医生问我上次在家量到「低烧」是什么时候。

words.enDefinition: a quick noticeable rise in body temperature

examples.en: I recorded a temperature spike just after dinner, when I'd been feeling cold.
examples.zh: 刚吃完晚饭，我明明觉得冷，却记录到「体温骤升」。

examples.en: The nurse asked how long the temperature spike had lasted before my appointment.
examples.zh: 护士问我来看诊前那次「体温骤升」持续了多久。

words.enDefinition: a sensation of cold that can cause shaking or shivering

examples.en: I had chills even though the room was warm and I wore a sweater.
examples.zh: 房间很暖，我也穿着毛衣，但我还是「发冷打寒战」。

examples.en: The chills began yesterday, halfway through my afternoon walk back from campus.
examples.zh: 「发冷寒战」是昨天开始的，当时我下午正走在回宿舍的路上。

words.enDefinition: episodes of sweating heavily while asleep

examples.en: I woke up with night sweats and found that my shirt and pillow were damp.
examples.zh: 我半夜因「夜间盗汗」醒来，发现上衣和枕头都潮了。

examples.en: The nurse asked how often the night sweats had woken me this month.
examples.zh: 护士问这个月我有多少次因为「夜间盗汗」醒过来。

words.enDefinition: sweating accompanied by a sudden feeling of cold

examples.en: I broke out in a cold sweat when the pain suddenly got worse.
examples.zh: 疼痛突然加剧时，我冒了一身「冷汗」。

examples.en: I woke up in a cold sweat shortly after the discomfort first started.
examples.zh: 不舒服刚出现没多久，我就冒着「冷汗」醒了过来。

collocations: break out in a cold sweat
wake up in a cold sweat
be covered in a cold sweat

words.enDefinition: skin that feels cool and slightly damp to touch

examples.en: My roommate noticed my clammy skin while we waited in the clinic lobby.
examples.zh: 我们在诊所大厅等候时，室友发现我的「皮肤又湿又冷」。

examples.en: I told the nurse about the clammy skin and when it first appeared.
examples.zh: 我告诉护士我的「皮肤湿冷」，并说了这种情况最早什么时候出现。

words.enDefinition: temporary redness of the face, often with warmth

examples.en: I noticed facial flushing halfway through the walk even though the weather was cool.
examples.zh: 虽然天气凉，我走到半路还是发现自己「脸部潮红」。

examples.en: The clinician asked whether the facial flushing felt hot or just looked red.
examples.zh: 医生问「脸部潮红」的时候我觉得发烫，还是只是看上去红。

words.enDefinition: soreness or pain felt in several parts of the body

examples.en: The body aches were worse in the evening, especially across my shoulders and legs.
examples.zh: 「全身酸痛」到晚上更厉害，尤其是肩膀和腿。

examples.en: I told the nurse that the body aches had lasted since Monday morning.
examples.zh: 我告诉护士，「全身酸痛」从星期一早上就开始了。

words.enDefinition: discomfort in one or more places where bones meet

examples.en: The joint pain is mostly in my knees and feels worse after climbing stairs.
examples.zh: 「关节疼痛」主要在膝盖，上下楼之后更厉害。

examples.en: The clinician asked if the joint pain was on both sides or only one.
examples.zh: 医生问「关节疼痛」是两边都有，还是只在一边。

words.enDefinition: joints that feel hard to bend or move freely

examples.en: I wake up with stiff joints, especially in my fingers, on colder mornings.
examples.zh: 早上天气冷的时候，我睡醒会觉得「关节僵硬」，手指尤其明显。

examples.en: The stiff joints make it harder for me to open jars in the morning.
examples.zh: 早上「关节僵硬」，我拧罐子盖会更吃力。

words.enDefinition: sudden painful tightening of muscles that you cannot control

examples.en: The muscle cramps woke me twice during the night and then stopped.
examples.zh: 我夜里两次被「肌肉抽筋」弄醒，后来就不抽了。

examples.en: I get muscle cramps in my calves after long periods of standing.
examples.zh: 我站久了，小腿「肌肉就会抽筋」。

words.enDefinition: small involuntary movements in a muscle or part of one

examples.en: I noticed muscle twitching in my eyelid while sitting quietly in the library.
examples.zh: 我安静坐在图书馆时，发现眼皮在不自主地「跳动」。

examples.en: The muscle twitching lasts a few seconds and comes back later in the day.
examples.zh: 「肌肉跳动」持续几秒，过一会儿当天还会出现。

words.enDefinition: a feeling of pressure or squeezing in the chest

examples.en: I noticed chest tightness while carrying my laundry up the stairs yesterday.
examples.zh: 昨天抱着衣服上楼时，我觉得「胸口发紧」。

examples.en: The nurse asked when the chest tightness began and how long it lasted.
examples.zh: 护士问我「胸口发紧」是什么时候开始的，持续了多久。

words.enDefinition: a neck that feels hard or painful to move

examples.en: I woke up with a stiff neck and found it hard to turn left.
examples.zh: 我醒来时「脖子僵硬」，很难把头转向左边。

examples.en: My stiff neck felt worse after sitting through the long lecture on Friday.
examples.zh: 星期五坐着听完一节长课后，我的「脖子更僵硬了」。

collocations: wake up with a stiff neck

words.enDefinition: painful when light pressure is applied to an area

examples.en: There's a spot on my shoulder that is tender to the touch.
examples.zh: 我肩膀上有个地方「一碰就疼」。

examples.en: I told the doctor that my ankle was still tender to the touch.
examples.zh: 我告诉医生，我的脚踝还是「一碰就疼」。

collocations: a spot tender to the touch

words.enDefinition: pain that starts or worsens when an area moves

examples.en: I get pain on movement when I try to reach for a top shelf.
examples.zh: 我伸手够最上层的架子时，会「一活动就疼」。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether I had pain on movement or only some stiffness.
examples.zh: 护士问我是「活动时疼痛」，还是只是有点僵硬。

collocations: pain on movement of the shoulder

words.enDefinition: pain present even when the body part is not moving

examples.en: I noticed pain at rest for the first time while sitting on the bus.
examples.zh: 我第一次「静止时感到疼痛」是在坐公交车的时候。

examples.en: The clinician asked if I had pain at rest or only while walking.
examples.zh: 医生问我是否「静止时也疼」，还是只有走路时疼。

words.enDefinition: pain that feels acute, pointed, or cutting

examples.en: I felt a sharp pain in my foot when I stepped off the bus.
examples.zh: 我下公交车时，脚上突然一阵「尖锐疼痛」。

examples.en: I get a sharp pain in my side whenever I bend to the right.
examples.zh: 我每次往右侧弯腰，身侧就会有「尖锐疼痛」。

collocations: a sharp pain in the side

words.enDefinition: a persistent low feeling of pain without a sharp edge

examples.en: I still had a dull ache in my back when I got home.
examples.zh: 我到家后，背上还是有一点「隐隐的钝痛」。

examples.en: What started as a dull ache became more noticeable later in the afternoon.
examples.zh: 最开始只是「隐隐的钝痛」，到了下午晚些时候就明显了。

collocations: a dull ache in the back

words.enDefinition: pain felt in repeated pulses or beats

examples.en: The throbbing pain near my temple made it hard to follow the lecture.
examples.zh: 太阳穴附近的「搏动性疼痛」让我很难跟上课。

examples.en: I described the throbbing pain to the doctor as beating in regular pulses.
examples.zh: 我向医生形容，「搏动性疼痛」就像有节奏地一跳一跳。

words.enDefinition: sudden pain that rapidly travels along part of the body

examples.en: I felt a shooting pain down my leg when I bent to tie my shoe.
examples.zh: 我弯腰系鞋带时，疼痛一下「窜到」了腿上。

examples.en: The shooting pain went from my shoulder to my elbow and quickly faded.
examples.zh: 这阵「窜痛」从肩膀传到手肘，很快就消退了。

words.enDefinition: pain that feels as if the area is burning

examples.en: The burning pain in my chest began shortly after I finished dinner.
examples.zh: 我刚吃完晚饭不久，胸口就出现了「烧灼样疼痛」。

examples.en: I told the nurse that the burning pain kept me awake last night.
examples.zh: 我告诉护士，昨晚的「烧灼样疼痛」让我一直睡不着。

collocations: a burning pain in the chest

words.enDefinition: pain that spreads from one area to another part

examples.en: The doctor asked where the radiating pain started and which way it went.
examples.zh: 医生问「放射痛」从哪里开始、往哪个方向扩散。

examples.en: I mentioned radiating pain from my lower back to the outside of my thigh.
examples.zh: 我提到从腰部到大腿外侧有「放射痛」。

words.enDefinition: pain confined to one specific small area of the body

examples.en: I have localized pain just below my ribs on the left side.
examples.zh: 我左侧肋骨正下方有「局部疼痛」。

examples.en: The localized pain has stayed in the same spot since I first noticed it.
examples.zh: 最初察觉后，「局部疼痛」一直在原来的位置。

words.enDefinition: pain that repeatedly tightens and relaxes like a cramp

examples.en: The cramping pain came in waves while I was sitting in the library.
examples.zh: 我坐在图书馆的时候，「痉挛性疼痛」一阵阵袭来。

examples.en: I told the nurse where I felt the cramping pain last night.
examples.zh: 我告诉护士，昨晚身体哪个部位有「痉挛性疼痛」。

words.enDefinition: pain that does not stop during the time described

examples.en: I have constant pain in my wrist, even when I'm not using it.
examples.zh: 我的手腕「一直疼」，即使不用它的时候也疼。

examples.en: The constant pain started three days ago and hasn't let up since.
examples.zh: 「持续不断的疼痛」三天前开始，此后一直没停。

collocations: constant pain in the lower back

words.enDefinition: pain that starts and stops over a period of time

examples.en: The intermittent pain in my knee often disappears before my morning lecture.
examples.zh: 我膝盖的「间歇性疼痛」常常在早课开始前就消失了。

examples.en: I marked the times of the intermittent pain to show the doctor.
examples.zh: 我记下「间歇性疼痛」发作的时间，准备给医生看。

words.enDefinition: pain that feels like pressing or squeezing against an area

examples.en: I described a pressure-like pain behind my eyes that lasted all afternoon.
examples.zh: 我形容说眼睛后面有「压迫样疼痛」，持续了一下午。

examples.en: The clinician asked how long the pressure-like pain near my chest lasted.
examples.zh: 医生问我胸口附近的「压迫样疼痛」持续了多久。

collocations: a pressure-like pain behind the eyes

words.enDefinition: the beginning of a symptom without a gradual buildup

examples.en: I mentioned the sudden onset of dizziness when the clinician asked about timing.
examples.zh: 医生问症状时间时，我提到头晕是「突然出现的」。

examples.en: We noted the sudden onset because she had felt fine all morning.
examples.zh: 我们记录了「突然起病」的情况，因为她整个上午都没觉得不舒服。

words.enDefinition: the slow appearance of a symptom over a period

examples.en: The gradual onset made it difficult to say exactly when I first felt tired.
examples.zh: 因为是「逐渐起病」，我很难说清最早是什么时候觉得疲倦。

examples.en: I described the gradual onset of the pain over several weeks of classes.
examples.zh: 我描述了几周上课期间疼痛如何「逐渐出现」。

words.enDefinition: become noticeably worse after being mild or calm

examples.en: My symptoms tend to flare up at night and settle by morning.
examples.zh: 我的症状往往夜里「突然加重」，到早上就缓解了。

examples.en: Sometimes the pain will flare up while I am just sitting still.
examples.zh: 有时我只是坐着不动，疼痛也会「突然加重」。

words.enDefinition: become less intense or less uncomfortable

examples.en: The pain began to ease up a few minutes after I sat down.
examples.zh: 我坐下几分钟后，疼痛就开始「有所缓解」。

examples.en: The cramps usually ease up by lunchtime, but the fatigue tends to linger.
examples.zh: 痉挛通常到了午饭时间会「有所缓解」，但疲倦往往还会持续。

collocations: wait for the cramps to ease up

words.enDefinition: affecting only the left side or only the right side

examples.en: The swelling is on one side of my face, mainly below my cheekbone.
examples.zh: 我的脸「只肿了一侧」，主要在颧骨下方。

examples.en: The nurse asked if the soreness was on one side of my back.
examples.zh: 护士问酸痛是不是「只在背部的一侧」。

words.enDefinition: in the area directly underneath the lowest ribs

examples.en: The ache is just below the ribs and stays in one spot.
examples.zh: 酸痛「就在肋骨下方」，一直在同一个地方。

examples.en: I pointed to a spot just below the ribs on my left side.
examples.zh: 我指了指左侧「就在肋骨下方」的一个位置。

collocations: feel pressure just below the ribs

words.enDefinition: the lower inward-curving area just above the buttocks

examples.en: The soreness is in the small of the back and feels worse when I stand.
examples.zh: 酸痛在「腰背部」，站起来时更明显。

examples.en: I felt a dull ache in the small of the back after my bus ride.
examples.zh: 坐完公交车后，我的「腰背部」隐隐作痛。

collocations: pain in the small of the back
stiffness in the small of the back
pressure on the small of the back

words.enDefinition: the bottom part of the skull where it meets the neck

examples.en: I feel pressure around the base of the skull when I look down.
examples.zh: 我低头时，觉得「颅底」附近有压迫感。

examples.en: The pain begins at the base of the skull and moves upward.
examples.zh: 疼痛从「颅底」开始，然后向上蔓延。

collocations: soreness at the base of the skull
pain at the base of the skull
tension near the base of the skull

words.enDefinition: the part of the belly above the navel

examples.en: I feel tightness in the upper abdomen, especially after a large meal.
examples.zh: 我觉得「上腹部」发紧，尤其是吃得多了以后。

examples.en: The nurse asked me to point to the upper abdomen where I felt discomfort.
examples.zh: 护士让我指出「上腹部」哪个位置不舒服。

words.enDefinition: pain in the belly area below the navel

examples.en: I noticed lower abdominal pain while walking back from my morning class.
examples.zh: 我早上下课往回走时，出现了「下腹部疼痛」。

examples.en: The lower abdominal pain was mild at first but got worse overnight.
examples.zh: 「下腹部疼痛」一开始很轻，但过了一夜变严重了。

words.enDefinition: sudden tightening pains felt in the belly

examples.en: I had stomach cramps on the bus just after leaving the dining hall.
examples.zh: 我刚离开食堂，在公交上突然「肚子绞痛」。

examples.en: The stomach cramps woke me up early, but they did not last long.
examples.zh: 我一大早被「肚子绞痛」弄醒，不过疼痛没持续多久。

words.enDefinition: minor discomfort in the stomach, often with nausea

examples.en: I had an upset stomach after lunch and didn't want much dinner.
examples.zh: 午饭后我有些「胃部不适」，晚饭就没什么胃口。

examples.en: My roommate mentioned an upset stomach after we got back from the trip.
examples.zh: 我们旅行回来后，室友说有些「胃部不适」。

words.enDefinition: have the uncomfortable feeling that you might vomit

examples.en: I started to feel queasy halfway through the long bus ride this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上坐长途公交到半路时，我开始「感觉恶心想吐」。

examples.en: I still feel queasy whenever I smell food from the cafeteria downstairs.
examples.zh: 只要闻到楼下食堂的饭菜味，我还是会「感觉恶心想吐」。

words.enDefinition: bring stomach contents back up through the mouth

examples.en: I felt like I might throw up during my walk to class.
examples.zh: 我走去上课的路上觉得自己可能要「吐」。

examples.en: It felt like I might throw up again just after getting home.
examples.zh: 我刚到家，就觉得可能又要「吐」了。

collocations: feel like you might throw up

words.enDefinition: the motions of vomiting without bringing up stomach contents

examples.en: I started dry heaving before breakfast, but nothing came up at all.
examples.zh: 早饭前我开始「干呕」，但什么也没吐出来。

examples.en: The nurse asked how long the dry heaving had lasted that morning.
examples.zh: 护士问我，那天早上的「干呕」持续了多久。

words.enDefinition: bowel movements that are softer or more watery than usual

examples.en: I have had loose stools for two days, mostly in the morning.
examples.zh: 这两天我有「稀便」，大多在早上。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether I had been having loose stools more often since yesterday.
examples.zh: 护士问我从昨天开始是不是更频繁地「排稀便」了。

words.enDefinition: blood present in stool, visible or detected by a test

examples.en: I noticed blood in the stool this morning and mentioned it during my appointment.
examples.zh: 我今天早上发现「便中带血」，看诊时把这件事告诉了医生。

examples.en: The clinician asked if I had seen blood in the stool before today.
examples.zh: 医生问我今天之前有没有发现过「便中带血」。

collocations: signs of blood in the stool

words.enDefinition: a feeling that the belly is unusually full or swollen

examples.en: The bloating is usually worse after dinner and better by the next morning.
examples.zh: 「腹胀」通常在晚饭后更严重，到第二天早上会好一些。

examples.en: I mentioned the bloating because my jeans felt tight by the afternoon.
examples.zh: 我提到「腹胀」，因为到了下午牛仔裤就开始勒得慌。

words.enDefinition: more gas than usual in the stomach or intestines

examples.en: I noticed excess gas throughout the afternoon and felt uncomfortable during class.
examples.zh: 整个下午我都觉得「肠胃胀气」，上课时很不舒服。

examples.en: The nurse asked when the excess gas first started and whether it came and went.
examples.zh: 护士问「肠胃胀气」是什么时候开始的，会不会时好时坏。

words.enDefinition: releasing gas from the stomach through the mouth

examples.en: I noticed more burping than usual after lunch at the student dining hall.
examples.zh: 我在学生食堂吃过午饭后，发现「嗳气」比平时多。

examples.en: I mentioned the burping when the nurse asked what happened after I ate.
examples.zh: 护士问我饭后有什么情况时，我提到了「嗳气」。

words.enDefinition: a burning feeling behind the breastbone or up the throat

examples.en: I sometimes get heartburn after dinner when I lie down too soon.
examples.zh: 有时晚饭后躺得太早，我会觉得「烧心」。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether the heartburn was worse at night or after meals.
examples.zh: 护士问我是夜里「烧心」更厉害，还是饭后更厉害。

words.enDefinition: an acidic taste that remains in the mouth

examples.en: I woke up with a sour taste in my mouth on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 星期二早上醒来时，我「嘴里有酸味」。

examples.en: The sour taste stayed in my mouth for several minutes after lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭过后，我「嘴里有酸味」，过了好几分钟才散。

collocations: a sour taste in the mouth

words.enDefinition: feeling unable to keep eating after a small amount

examples.en: I mentioned feeling full quickly, even after only a few bites of dinner.
examples.zh: 我提到自己「很快就有饱腹感」，晚饭才吃几口就饱了。

examples.en: Feeling full quickly has made it hard to finish my lunches this week.
examples.zh: 因为「很快就有饱腹感」，这周我很难吃完午饭。

collocations: feeling full quickly after starting a meal

words.enDefinition: cannot eat without vomiting afterward

examples.en: I told my flatmate I can't keep food down even when I eat slowly.
examples.zh: 我跟室友说，哪怕慢慢吃，我也「吃什么都吐」。

examples.en: I told the nurse I can't keep food down, even after a very small breakfast.
examples.zh: 我告诉护士，我才吃了一点早饭，还是「吃什么都吐」。

collocations: say you can't keep food down
notice you can't keep food down

words.enDefinition: needing to pass urine more often than usual

examples.en: I noticed frequent urination after waking twice to use the bathroom last night.
examples.zh: 昨晚我起来去了两次厕所，这才留意到自己「尿频」。

examples.en: The clinician asked whether the frequent urination happened during the day as well.
examples.zh: 医生问白天是不是也有「尿频」。

words.enDefinition: pain or discomfort that happens while passing urine

examples.en: I told the nurse that the painful urination had started the previous evening.
examples.zh: 我告诉护士，「排尿时疼痛」是前一天晚上开始的。

examples.en: The clinician asked whether the painful urination stopped once I left the bathroom.
examples.zh: 医生问「排尿时的疼痛」是不是在离开厕所后就消失了。

words.enDefinition: a strong sudden need to pass urine without delay

examples.en: I felt an urgent need to urinate halfway through my afternoon lecture.
examples.zh: 下午的课听到一半，我突然「尿急」。

examples.en: The urgent need to urinate returned even after I had used the bathroom.
examples.zh: 即使刚上完厕所，我又开始「尿急」。

collocations: feel an urgent need to urinate
report an urgent need to urinate
a repeated urgent need to urinate

words.enDefinition: blood present in urine, visible or detected by a test

examples.en: I noticed blood in the urine for the first time on Tuesday morning.
examples.zh: 我星期二早上第一次发现「尿中带血」。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether the blood in the urine had appeared more than once.
examples.zh: 护士问「尿中带血」是不是出现过不止一次。

collocations: check for blood in the urine

words.enDefinition: the unintentional passage of urine

examples.en: I noticed urine leakage for the first time after a long walk.
examples.zh: 我走了很久以后，第一次发现自己有「漏尿」。

examples.en: The nurse asked when the urine leakage happened and whether I noticed it immediately.
examples.zh: 护士问「漏尿」是何时发生的，我有没有马上察觉。

words.enDefinition: painful cramps associated with a menstrual period

examples.en: My period cramps were worse than usual during my afternoon class yesterday.
examples.zh: 昨天下午上课时，我的「经期腹痛」比平时更厉害。

examples.en: I noted when my period cramps started and when they began to ease.
examples.zh: 我记下了「经期腹痛」何时开始、何时开始缓解。

collocations: get period cramps in the morning

words.zhGloss: 两次月经间的点滴出血
words.enDefinition: light vaginal bleeding in the time between menstrual periods
acceptedZhAnswers: 两次月经间的点滴出血

examples.en: I noticed spotting between periods for the first time during my field placement.
examples.zh: 我在外实习期间，第一次发现「两次月经间有点滴出血」。

examples.en: The clinician asked when the spotting between periods had first appeared this month.
examples.zh: 医生问我这个月「两次月经间的点滴出血」最早是什么时候出现的。

words.enDefinition: a strong headache that feels like repeated or heavy blows

examples.en: I woke up with a pounding headache and turned off my alarm.
examples.zh: 我醒来后觉得「头一跳一跳地疼得厉害」，就关掉了闹钟。

examples.en: The pounding headache started on the train and lasted until I reached home.
examples.zh: 「剧烈的跳动性头痛」从火车上开始，一直到我回家才结束。

collocations: wake up with a pounding headache

words.enDefinition: a feeling of unsteadiness, spinning, or possible fainting

examples.en: I felt some dizziness after standing up quickly during the library group meeting.
examples.zh: 图书馆小组开会时，我猛地站起来，感觉有点「头晕」。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether the dizziness had happened while I was sitting down.
examples.zh: 护士问我是不是坐着的时候也会「头晕」。

words.enDefinition: feel weak or dizzy as if you could faint

examples.en: I sometimes feel lightheaded when I stand up after a long lecture.
examples.zh: 坐着听完一节长课后，有时站起来会觉得「头晕发飘」。

examples.en: I began to feel lightheaded while waiting in the student centre for my friend.
examples.zh: 我在学生活动中心等朋友时，开始觉得「头晕发飘」。

collocations: feel lightheaded in a warm room

words.enDefinition: a brief episode in which someone loses consciousness

examples.en: I had a fainting spell in the hallway before my morning seminar.
examples.zh: 上午的研讨课还没开始，我在走廊里「短暂晕厥了一次」。

examples.en: My roommate described the fainting spell because I couldn't remember what had happened.
examples.zh: 我记不清发生了什么，室友描述了那次「短暂晕厥」。

words.enDefinition: feel unable to balance steadily while standing or walking

examples.en: I feel unsteady for a moment when I first get out of bed.
examples.zh: 我刚下床时，会有一会儿「感觉站不稳」。

examples.en: The clinician asked when I began to feel unsteady on the stairs.
examples.zh: 医生问我什么时候开始在楼梯上「感觉走不稳」。

words.enDefinition: the sensation that you or your surroundings are moving or spinning

examples.en: I described the vertigo as feeling like the room was spinning around me.
examples.zh: 我形容「眩晕」的感觉，就像整间屋子绕着我转。

examples.en: The vertigo began while I was lying completely still in my room.
examples.zh: 我一动不动地躺在房间里时，突然出现了「眩晕」。

words.enDefinition: a prickling feeling like many tiny needles against the skin

examples.en: I started getting pins and needles in my foot during the film.
examples.zh: 看电影时，我的脚开始有「针刺样麻感」。

examples.en: The pins and needles faded after a few minutes but returned before lunch.
examples.zh: 「针刺样麻感」几分钟后消失了，但午饭前又出现了。

collocations: pins and needles in my hand

words.enDefinition: partial or complete loss of normal feeling in an area

examples.en: I noticed numbness in two of my fingers halfway through the lecture.
examples.zh: 课听到一半，我发现两根手指「麻木」了。

examples.en: The clinician asked whether the numbness had spread to my left hand.
examples.zh: 医生问「麻木」有没有蔓延到我的左手。

words.enDefinition: hands that shake in repeated movements without your intending it

examples.en: I had shaky hands for several minutes after my morning lab session.
examples.zh: 上午实验课结束后，我的「手发抖」了好几分钟。

examples.en: I noticed my shaky hands when I tried to open a small envelope.
examples.zh: 我想打开一个小信封时，才注意到「手在发抖」。

words.enDefinition: a feeling of mental cloudiness that makes thinking harder

examples.en: The brain fog made it hard to follow the reading this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上「脑子昏沉」，我很难读懂手头的材料。

examples.en: I described the brain fog as feeling slow and muddled throughout the day.
examples.zh: 我描述了「脑子昏沉」的感觉，就是一整天思路都迟缓又混乱。

words.enDefinition: difficulty keeping your attention on one activity or thought

examples.en: I have trouble concentrating on my notes when the headache is particularly bad.
examples.zh: 头疼得特别厉害时，我「难以集中注意力」看笔记。

examples.en: I noticed trouble concentrating at home even when my room was completely quiet.
examples.zh: 即使家里的房间非常安静，我还是发现自己「难以集中注意力」。

words.enDefinition: speaking with words that sound unclear or run together

examples.en: My roommate noticed slurred speech while I was describing what had happened.
examples.zh: 我描述当时发生的事时，室友注意到我「口齿含糊」。

examples.en: I told the clinician how long the slurred speech had lasted that morning.
examples.zh: 我告诉医生，那天早上「口齿含糊」持续了多久。

words.enDefinition: drooping of part of the face, often on one side

examples.en: My friend noticed a facial droop on my right side while we were talking.
examples.zh: 聊天时，朋友注意到我的右侧「面部下垂」。

examples.en: The nurse asked when the facial droop first became visible to my roommate.
examples.zh: 护士问我室友最早是什么时候看见我「面部下垂」的。

words.enDefinition: feeling discomfort from light that others might tolerate easily

examples.en: I noticed sensitivity to light when I stepped outside after my lecture.
examples.zh: 下课走到室外时，我觉得自己「对光敏感」。

examples.en: The sensitivity to light made the bright library lights especially uncomfortable yesterday.
examples.zh: 昨天因为「对光敏感」，图书馆明亮的灯光让我很不舒服。

words.enDefinition: finding ordinary sounds unusually loud, painful, or uncomfortable

examples.en: My sensitivity to noise became more noticeable in the busy dining hall.
examples.zh: 在嘈杂的食堂里，我「对声音更敏感了」。

examples.en: The clinician asked if the sensitivity to noise started before the headache.
examples.zh: 医生问我是不是头疼前就开始「对声音敏感」。

words.enDefinition: a cough that does not bring up mucus

examples.en: I developed a dry cough halfway through the week of my exams.
examples.zh: 我那周考到一半时，开始「干咳」。

examples.en: The dry cough usually starts after I lie down for the night.
examples.zh: 我晚上躺下后通常就会开始「干咳」。

words.enDefinition: bring mucus out of the airways by coughing

examples.en: I cough up mucus most mornings before I leave for my first class.
examples.zh: 我大多数早晨出门上第一节课之前，都会「咳出痰」。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether I cough up mucus or just have a dry cough.
examples.zh: 护士问我会不会「咳出痰」，还是只是干咳。

collocations: cough up mucus in the morning

words.enDefinition: a spell of repeated coughing that is difficult to stop

examples.en: I had a coughing fit during the lecture and stepped into the hallway.
examples.zh: 上课时我「一阵猛咳」，就走到了走廊里。

examples.en: The coughing fit lasted several minutes before I could speak clearly again.
examples.zh: 我「一阵猛咳」，过了几分钟才能重新说清楚话。

words.enDefinition: a throat that feels dry, irritated, or slightly rough

examples.en: I woke up with a scratchy throat but could still talk normally.
examples.zh: 我醒来时「喉咙干痒」，但还是能正常说话。

examples.en: The scratchy throat bothered me most when I read aloud in class.
examples.zh: 「喉咙干痒」在我上课朗读时最难受。

collocations: wake up with a scratchy throat

words.enDefinition: enlarged lymph nodes that may be felt under the skin

examples.en: I noticed swollen glands beneath my jaw while I was washing my face.
examples.zh: 我洗脸时发现下巴下面有「淋巴结肿大」。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether the swollen glands were painful when I touched them.
examples.zh: 护士问我，碰到「肿大的淋巴结」时是否觉得痛。

words.enDefinition: pain felt while swallowing food, drink, or saliva

examples.en: I noticed pain when swallowing even though my voice still sounded normal.
examples.zh: 虽然声音听上去还是正常的，但我发现自己「吞咽时疼痛」。

examples.en: I told the clinician that the pain when swallowing was worse in the morning.
examples.zh: 我告诉医生，早上「吞咽时疼痛」更明显。

words.enDefinition: trouble moving food, liquid, or saliva down the throat

examples.en: I had difficulty swallowing bread at lunch but could still drink water.
examples.zh: 午饭吃面包时，我觉得「吞咽困难」，不过还是能喝水。

examples.en: The clinician asked how long the difficulty swallowing had been troubling me.
examples.zh: 医生问这种「吞咽困难」困扰我多久了。

words.enDefinition: a speaking voice that sounds rough, weak, or strained

examples.en: I woke up with a hoarse voice on the day of my presentation.
examples.zh: 我在做汇报的当天醒来时，发现自己「声音沙哑」。

examples.en: The nurse asked if the hoarse voice had sounded worse after class yesterday.
examples.zh: 护士问我昨天下课后，「声音沙哑」有没有更明显。

collocations: wake up with a hoarse voice

words.enDefinition: a nose that releases more fluid or mucus than usual

examples.en: I had a runny nose throughout the afternoon, especially on the walk home.
examples.zh: 我一下午都在「流鼻涕」，走回家的路上尤其明显。

examples.en: The runny nose started before I noticed any discomfort in my throat.
examples.zh: 我先开始「流鼻涕」，后来才觉得喉咙不舒服。

words.enDefinition: a nose that feels blocked and hard to breathe through

examples.en: I woke up with a stuffy nose after falling asleep on the train.
examples.zh: 我在火车上睡着了，醒来时觉得「鼻塞」。

examples.en: The stuffy nose was worse last night, but the cough had stayed the same.
examples.zh: 昨晚「鼻塞」更严重了，咳嗽却和之前一样。

collocations: wake up with a stuffy nose

words.enDefinition: mucus draining from the back of the nose into the throat

examples.en: I described the postnasal drip as a trickling feeling behind my throat.
examples.zh: 我形容「鼻涕倒流」时，觉得有东西沿着喉咙后方往下流。

examples.en: The postnasal drip was more noticeable once I lay down at night.
examples.zh: 晚上躺下以后，「鼻涕倒流」就更明显了。

words.enDefinition: a sensation of fullness or pressure in the sinus area

examples.en: I felt sinus pressure around my cheeks when I bent to pick up my bag.
examples.zh: 我弯腰捡包时，觉得脸颊附近有「鼻窦压迫感」。

examples.en: The sinus pressure grew more noticeable in the afternoon and eased before dinner.
examples.zh: 「鼻窦压迫感」下午更明显，到晚饭前才缓解。

words.enDefinition: bleeding from inside one or both sides of the nose

examples.en: I had a nosebleed on the bus and missed the start of class.
examples.zh: 我在公交上「鼻出血」，错过了课程的开头。

examples.en: The nurse asked how long the nosebleed lasted and whether it happened before.
examples.zh: 护士问「鼻出血」持续了多久，以前有没有出现过。

words.enDefinition: a reduced or absent ability to detect smells

examples.en: I first noticed the loss of smell when I opened a bag of coffee.
examples.zh: 我打开一袋咖啡时，第一次发现自己「闻不出味道」了。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether the loss of smell had lasted more than one day.
examples.zh: 护士问「嗅觉减退或丧失」是否持续了一天以上。

collocations: report a sudden loss of smell

words.enDefinition: a reduced or absent ability to detect basic tastes

examples.en: I noticed a loss of taste when my very salty soup seemed plain.
examples.zh: 很咸的汤喝起来却很淡，我这才注意到自己「味觉减退」了。

examples.en: The clinician asked when the loss of taste started and whether it was complete.
examples.zh: 医生问「味觉减退或丧失」从什么时候开始，以及是不是完全尝不出味道。

words.enDefinition: feeling unable to get enough air or breathe comfortably

examples.en: I noticed shortness of breath while walking uphill to the lecture hall.
examples.zh: 我上坡走去报告厅时，觉得有些「气短」。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether I had shortness of breath even while sitting.
examples.zh: 护士问我坐着时是不是也会「气短」。

words.enDefinition: a high whistling sound that occurs as someone breathes

examples.en: I noticed wheezing when I breathed out after walking home last night.
examples.zh: 昨晚走回家后，我注意到自己「呼气有哨声」。

examples.en: The clinician asked if the wheezing was more noticeable at night or during exercise.
examples.zh: 医生问我的「呼吸哨声」是夜间更明显，还是运动时更明显。

words.enDefinition: taking small breaths without drawing much air each time

examples.en: My friend noticed shallow breathing while I was sitting on the bench.
examples.zh: 我坐在长椅上时，朋友注意到我「呼吸很浅」。

examples.en: The nurse asked how long the shallow breathing had continued after I sat down.
examples.zh: 护士问我坐下后，「呼吸浅」的情况持续了多久。

words.enDefinition: a sensation that the heart is beating much faster than usual

examples.en: I woke up with a racing heart and felt wide awake immediately.
examples.zh: 我醒来时「心跳很快」，一下子就完全清醒了。

examples.en: I mentioned a racing heart while describing what happened on the bus.
examples.zh: 我描述公交上发生的事时，提到了当时「心跳很快」。

collocations: wake up with a racing heart

words.enDefinition: a sensation that one heartbeat is missing or delayed

examples.en: I noticed what felt like a skipped heartbeat while lying in bed.
examples.zh: 我躺在床上时，感觉「心跳像是漏了一拍」。

examples.en: The clinician asked when I had first noticed the occasional skipped heartbeat.
examples.zh: 医生问我什么时候开始察觉偶尔「心跳漏一拍」。

words.enDefinition: ankles that have become larger or puffy than usual

examples.en: I noticed swollen ankles after taking off my shoes on Friday evening.
examples.zh: 星期五晚上脱鞋后，我发现自己「脚踝肿胀」。

examples.en: The clinician asked whether my swollen ankles looked the same in the morning.
examples.zh: 医生问我早上的「脚踝肿胀」是不是也这么明显。

words.enDefinition: skin that produces a strong urge to scratch

examples.en: I have itchy skin on my arms that gets worse at night.
examples.zh: 我的手臂「皮肤发痒」，而且到了晚上更明显。

examples.en: The nurse asked how long I had noticed the itchy skin on my back.
examples.zh: 护士问我发现背上的「皮肤发痒」多久了。

words.enDefinition: skin shedding small visible pieces from its surface

examples.en: I noticed flaky skin around my nose while getting ready for class.
examples.zh: 我准备去上课时，发现鼻子周围「皮肤起屑」。

examples.en: The flaky skin on my hands first appeared early in the semester.
examples.zh: 我手上「皮肤起屑」的情况在学期刚开始时就出现了。

words.enDefinition: a visible change in skin color or texture over an area

examples.en: I noticed a skin rash on my arm while getting dressed this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上穿衣服的时候，我发现手臂上有「皮疹」。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether the skin rash had spread since I first saw it.
examples.zh: 护士问我最初发现后，「皮疹」有没有扩散。

words.enDefinition: raised itchy areas of skin that appear as welts

examples.en: I noticed hives on both arms when I changed my shirt after class.
examples.zh: 下课后换衬衫时，我发现两条手臂上都起了「风团」。

examples.en: I took a photo of the hives before they faded later that afternoon.
examples.zh: 当天下午「风团」消退前，我拍了张照片。

words.enDefinition: the formation of small sacs of fluid on skin

examples.en: I noticed blistering on one heel after taking off my walking boots.
examples.zh: 脱掉徒步靴后，我发现一边脚后跟「起水疱」了。

examples.en: The nurse asked when the blistering started and where I'd first seen it.
examples.zh: 护士问「起水疱」是什么时候开始的，我最早在哪里看到它。

words.enDefinition: discolored skin marks that appear without a known injury

examples.en: I noticed unexplained bruises on my shins while getting ready for bed.
examples.zh: 我准备上床时，注意到小腿有几处「不明原因的瘀青」。

examples.en: The clinician asked how often I had seen unexplained bruises that month.
examples.zh: 医生问那个月我多频繁地发现「不明原因的瘀青」。

words.enDefinition: a feeling of heat or stinging in one area

examples.en: I felt a burning sensation across the back of my hand yesterday.
examples.zh: 昨天我感觉手背上有一阵「灼烧感」。

examples.en: The nurse asked if the burning sensation was still there after dinner.
examples.zh: 护士问我吃完晚饭后还有没有「灼烧感」。

words.enDefinition: a change in the skin toward a yellow color

examples.en: My flatmate noticed yellowing of the skin around my face in daylight.
examples.zh: 在日光下，室友注意到我脸上的「皮肤发黄」。

examples.en: I mentioned the yellowing of the skin when my clinician asked about recent changes.
examples.zh: 医生问我最近有什么变化时，我提到了「皮肤发黄」。

words.enDefinition: a feeling of unusual dryness inside the mouth

examples.en: I woke up with dry mouth several times during the night last week.
examples.zh: 上周夜里我好几次因为「口干」醒来。

examples.en: I told the clinician that the dry mouth was most noticeable in the morning.
examples.zh: 我告诉医生，早上「口干」最明显。

words.enDefinition: feeling a much stronger need to drink than usual

examples.en: I noticed excessive thirst even though I'd already finished my water bottle.
examples.zh: 我把一整瓶水喝完了，还是觉得「异常口渴」。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether the excessive thirst continued after I left the gym.
examples.zh: 护士问我离开健身房后，是不是还是「异常口渴」。

words.enDefinition: difficulty passing stool or passing it less often than usual

examples.en: I mentioned the constipation when the nurse asked about changes during my trip.
examples.zh: 护士问我旅途中身体有什么变化时，我提到了「便秘」。

examples.en: The clinician asked how long the constipation had continued since I came home.
examples.zh: 医生问我回家后，「便秘」持续了多久。

words.enDefinition: frequent bowel movements that are loose or watery

examples.en: I had diarrhea several times on Saturday and noted when it began.
examples.zh: 我星期六「腹泻」了好几次，并记下了开始的时间。

examples.en: The nurse asked if the diarrhea made me leave class more than once.
examples.zh: 护士问我是不是因为「腹泻」好几次离开课堂。

words.enDefinition: trouble getting to sleep after trying to do so

examples.en: I had difficulty falling asleep because the pain in my shoulder kept returning.
examples.zh: 由于肩膀的疼痛反复出现，我「入睡困难」。

examples.en: The doctor asked when I first noticed difficulty falling asleep after moving here.
examples.zh: 医生问我搬来以后，最早什么时候开始出现「入睡困难」。

words.enDefinition: sleep that does not leave you feeling rested afterward

examples.en: I've had unrefreshing sleep all week despite going to bed early every night.
examples.zh: 尽管每晚都早睡，这周我却「睡醒后仍不解乏」。

examples.en: I described several nights of unrefreshing sleep even though I hadn't woken up once.
examples.zh: 我说虽然夜里一次都没醒过，但连续好几晚「睡醒后仍不解乏」。

words.enDefinition: symptoms that return after being absent for some time

examples.en: The clinician asked whether my recurrent symptoms followed the same pattern over time.
examples.zh: 医生问我这些「反复出现的症状」每次出现时表现是不是一样。

examples.en: I wrote down the recurrent symptoms before my appointment so I wouldn't forget them.
examples.zh: 看诊前我把「反复出现的症状」记了下来，免得忘记。

words.enDefinition: experiencing none of the symptoms being discussed

examples.en: I was symptom-free for nearly a week, and then the aches returned.
examples.zh: 我将近一个星期「没有症状」，然后酸痛又出现了。

examples.en: The nurse asked how long I had been symptom-free before the cough came back.
examples.zh: 护士问我咳嗽再次出现之前，有多久「没有症状」。

words.enDefinition: a way of rating the intensity of pain

examples.en: The nurse used a pain scale with numbers from zero to ten.
examples.zh: 护士用了一个从零到十的「疼痛评分量表」。

examples.en: I pointed to the pain scale to show how bad it felt.
examples.zh: 我指着「疼痛评分量表」，说明我觉得有多疼。

words.enDefinition: a record of when symptoms occur and how they feel

examples.en: I took my symptom diary to the appointment to show when the cramps started.
examples.zh: 我带着「症状日记」去看诊，说明痉挛是从什么时候开始的。

examples.en: My symptom diary shows that the dizziness usually lasts only a few minutes.
examples.zh: 我的「症状日记」显示，头晕通常只持续几分钟。

words.enDefinition: make it harder to do things you normally do

examples.en: The clinician asked whether the cramps affect daily activities such as cooking or walking.
examples.zh: 医生问痉挛是否「影响日常活动」，比如做饭或走路。

examples.en: I said the pain can affect daily activities on the days it lasts longer.
examples.zh: 我说疼痛持续时间较长的那些天，可能会「影响日常活动」。

words.enDefinition: happening more often now than before

examples.en: The headaches are getting more frequent, though they still go away quickly.
examples.zh: 头痛「发生得越来越频繁」，不过还是很快就会消失。

examples.en: I told the nurse the cramps were getting more frequent this week.
examples.zh: 我告诉护士，这周痉挛「发生得越来越频繁」。

words.enDefinition: while putting your body's weight on a particular limb

examples.en: My foot mainly hurts when bearing weight, such as while climbing stairs.
examples.zh: 我的脚主要在「负重时」疼，比如上楼时。

examples.en: The clinician asked if I felt tightness only when bearing weight on that leg.
examples.zh: 医生问我是不是只有那条腿「负重时」才会发紧。

words.enDefinition: at the time you draw a large breath in

examples.en: I get a sharp pain under my ribs when taking a deep breath.
examples.zh: 我在「深呼吸时」肋骨下面会突然疼一下。

examples.en: The nurse asked if I noticed more pain when taking a deep breath.
examples.zh: 护士问我「深呼吸时」疼痛会不会加剧。

collocations: hurt when taking a deep breath
feel discomfort when taking a deep breath
tightness when taking a deep breath
